evidence_quote: [![](https://journalmbr.com.br/public/journals/1/pageHeaderLogoImage_pt_BR.jpg)]( https://journalmbr.com.br/index.php/jmbr/index ) # Análise epidemiológica da Dengue no Brasil: uma série histórica 10 anos (2014 - 2024) ## Authors * Sarah Correa Soler Albino Titz de Rezende UNICID <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2691-1999> * Octávio Correa Soler Albino Pontifícia Universidade Católica (PUC Minas Gerais) ## DOI: <https://doi.org/10.70164/jmbr.v2i1.427> ## Keywords: Dengue, Epidemiologia, Série Histórica, Medicina Preventiva. ## Abstract the study analyzed dengue in Brazil from 2014 to 2024, using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) and government programs such as the Dengue Program and monitoring by the São Paulo government. Through descriptive statistical techniques, confirmed dengue cases, hospitalizations, and deaths were characterized, segmented by region, age group, and gender. Frequency tables, graphs, and maps facilitated the understanding of annual and regional trends and the geographical distribution of the disease. The analyses were performed using Microsoft Excel 365 (2023). The results show significant variations in the distribution of reported cases. The Southeast region predominated in notifications, particularly in 2015, representing 61.93% of cases, and in 2024, with an estimated 64.33%. The Midwest recorded a high incidence in 2018 (40.28%), while the Northeast stood out in 2022, with 32.43% of cases. The South showed growth in cases starting in 2022, reaching 25.86% in 2023. These regional fluctuations highlight the need for specific preventive approaches. The high incidence and recurrent outbreaks pressured the public health system, underscoring the need to strengthen dengue control strategies.
